title: How Commerce.com and Cloudflare are getting storefronts ready for AI agents
summary: Almost 100,000 Commerce.com domains now give AI agents real shopping tools through WebMCP on Cloudflare. Here's how we turned it on across every store at once, while keeping each merchant in control.

title: Cutting our inference bill by 68% by being obsessive about optimization
summary: When our AI code reviewer's cost per run doubled, we dug into the token usage to find out why. Learn how we used prompt caching and intelligent model routing to slash our inference bill by 68% while speeding up reviews.

title: Introducing Clairic, a new System One class of extraction models
summary: Clairic is a new model from Cloudflare that is a System One extraction modeI, capable of extracting, computing, estimating, and forecasting data from unstructured inputs.

title: Continuous accountability for Verified bots
summary: Identity alone doesn't guarantee a bot will behave responsibly. We are introducing a system to continuously evaluate whether Verified bots honor site preferences, like robots.txt and HTTP 429s, ensuring they remain accountable over time.

title: Cloudflare and OpenAI: Making AI discovery better for everyone
summary: How Cloudflare and OpenAI are working together to help AI find useful content, keep up with changes, and make fewer wasted requests — making the experience better for users and website owners alike.

title: Introducing Clef-omni with full multimodality, plus a faster Clef and a cheaper Clef-flash
summary: We are expanding the Clef decision model family with Clef-omni, natively processing audio, video, images, and text in a single pipeline. We’ve also lowered Clef-flash pricing and boosted Clef inference speeds by up to 2.0x.

title: Everything we launched during Birthday Week 2026
summary: We celebrated our 16th birthday with 46 announcements across open source, post-quantum security, AI agents, and developer platform upgrades. Here’s a day-by-day roundup of everything we shipped.

title: Introducing Web Search API via AI Gateway
summary: Cloudflare AI Gateway now supports native web search API integration in partnership with Ceramic.ai, Exa, and Linkup. Developers can now inject real-time web context into model inference calls via AI Gateway, REST APIs, or Workers bindings.

title: Building for good: How civil society organizations are automating on Cloudflare
summary: Some of the world's leading organizations are building the future of non-profit work with Cloudflare.

title: Introducing Clef: our open-source decision models, and new RL fine-tuning platform
summary: We are introducing Clef and Clef-flash, open-source decision models hosted on Workers AI for high-speed classification and agentic workflows. Also launching: a new reinforcement learning platform that allows developers to fine-tune decision models using their own data.

title: One year later: Sovereign AI and the fight for choice
summary: AI sovereignty is not a zero-sum game, but many governments now believe it is. Cloudflare's answer: more local open-source models, model-agnostic security tools, and a commitment to giving nations genuine choice.

title: Cloudflare OS: your company’s agent workspace, managed for you
summary: Cloudflare OS gives everyone in your organization an agent workspace that knows how your company works and connects to its data and systems. We’re opening the waitlist for fully managed deployments that you’ll be able to launch in a few clicks.

title: AI Search is now generally available
summary: AI Search is now generally available. It embeds image pixels directly for visual search, runs optical character recognition on scanned PDFs, accepts files up to 10 MiB, and works with any chat model. Here's what's new and how pricing works.

title: Cut your AI spend with AI Gateway's Auto Router
summary: Cloudflare AI Gateway now features a model router that evaluates request complexity using an edge-deployed classifier to select the optimal model. By balancing expected output quality against token costs, organizations can dramatically cut AI spend while maintaining performance.

title: Simplifying domains for people and agents
summary: Cloudflare Registrar’s new search delivers fast, transparent results across 420+ extensions using Workers, Durable Objects, and WebSockets. Its expanded API and cf CLI also let agents search, register, and transfer domains.

title: Monetization Gateway beta: charge AI agents for consumption with HTTP 402
summary: Cloudflare’s AI Gateway, Ceramic.ai, Stocktwits, and more are using the Cloudflare Monetization Gateway today to charge agents for access to tokens, APIs, and MCP tools. U.S.-based sellers can now apply for access to the closed beta.

title: Pay Per Use: when AI uses your work, you should get paid
summary: Pay Per Use is now in beta. AI companies report when they use publishers’ content, and Cloudflare handles billing, payouts, and reporting, so our customers are paid according to use.

title: Identify AI model overuse with User Insights
summary: AI Gateway User Insights now adds task, model, turn, and user categories to help teams understand AI adoption and make better model decisions. This is available free to AI Gateway users.

title: Cloudflare Containers, rebuilt to scale agent sandboxes
summary: Cloudflare Containers now start 6x faster, let your agent choose each sandbox's image and instance type at runtime, and support filesystem snapshots in public beta, all controlled from a Durable Object.

title: The Internet has a second audience
summary: More than half the traffic reaching sites on Cloudflare is now automated, and AI agents are the fastest-growing part of it. We're giving site owners the tools to see who's visiting, decide who gets in, and charge for access.

title: Protected Quick Tunnels: simple accountless authentication for your next dev project
summary: Quick Tunnels now support email authentication. Add --allowed-mail to one cloudflared command, and only the addresses or domains you list can reach your local app. No Cloudflare account required on either side.

summary: Misconfiguring Turnstile by skipping backend validation leaves sites exposed to bots. Turnstile Spin fixes incomplete setups by using your preferred AI coding agent to wire up server-side verification.

summary: Cloudflare OAuth now supports optional scopes, giving users more control over what an app can access and helping developers build secure consent flows around the task at hand.

title: Everything we launched during Agents Week

title: Unveiling good and bad behaviors on the Agentic Internet

Learn how new good and bad behaviors from bots and agents are assessed by our systems, including BotBase and Precursor — and try out our Precursor Trace simulation to see how your own cursor movements would be assessed as human or bot.

summary: Cloudflare Radar Researcher is a new AI-powered tool that lets you explore global Internet trends and traffic data using plain language. Built entirely on Cloudflare's Developer Platform, it turns natural language queries into real, interactive charts.

summary: We are launching updated community programs, including Cloudflare Ambassadors and Community Engineers, backed by $1M in open-source funding. Learn how we are supporting maintainers and scaling our developer community.

title: Unifying Workers AI and AI Gateway into a single AI control plane
summary: Cloudflare is unifying AI Gateway and Workers AI into a single control plane, giving developers observability, billing, and dynamic routing across both managed GPUs and external providers. Learn how unified bindings and model-first routing simplify building resilient AI applications.

title: Cloudflare AI Search: give your agents a search engine for your data
summary: AI Search makes search easier than ever, with no Cloudflare primitives to stitch together. Point it at your data to create a search for your own files and websites. We're also sharing a preview of our new pricing model.

title: The next generation of MCP
summary: The next version of MCP has a rewritten, stateless core that just works on Workers. We cover upgrades to the protocol, the new feature lifecycle and SDK migration path, and hear from early adopters already running it in production.

title: From ranking to recommended: get your site ready to thrive in the age of AI agents
summary: More than half of requests now come from machines, not people. Agent Readiness shows how well agents can discover and read your site, while Answer Engine Optimization tracks how often AI assistants recommend you.

title: Building an open Agentic Internet: readable, discoverable, callable, and payable
summary: Agents are a new kind of visitor. They don't render CSS or click ads, but they have a paying human on the other end. Block them and you block your customer. We're building the open tools and protocols so publishers and agents can cooperate and not collide.

title: Introducing Kitesurf: The agent-first browser that runs in V8 isolates on Cloudflare Workers
summary: We should be giving all agents tools that excel at what’s important for an AI model. Kitesurf is Cloudflare’s new stateless, highly scalable, and cost-effective web browser that runs entirely on top of Workers and was designed specifically for the Agentic Cloud.

title: VoidZero is joining Cloudflare
summary: VoidZero, the team behind Vite, Vitest, Rolldown, Oxc, and Vite+, is joining Cloudflare. Vite stays open source, vendor-agnostic, and built for everyone.

summary: We built our internal AI engineering stack on the same products we ship. That means 20 million requests routed through AI Gateway, 241 billion tokens processed, and inference running on Workers AI, serving more than 3,683 internal users. Here's how we did it.

title: v0.32.0
summary:
v0.32.0

Highlights

This release features 814 commits from 363 contributors (121 new)!

  • Structured decisions and generic parsers: the new POST /v1/systemone endpoint answers choice, noul and score questions over a structured state (#59299), is served by default (#60677, #60696), and also runs on Cloudflare/clef-omni (#61064), LiquidAI/d1-3B (#60676) and DiffusionGemma (#60466). The new hf tool and reasoning parser (--tool-call-parser hf, --reasoning-parser hf) reads the checkpoint's response_template, so models that ship it need no model-specific parser (#58604, #58602), in both the Python and Rust frontends (#59005).
  • Low-precision KV cache everywhere: NVFP4 KV cache now runs on SM8x and SM12x (#46963), SM90 (#60620) and with XQA decode on SM12x (#60452), and on MiniMax-M3 sparse attention on SM100 (#59300); GLM-5.x defaults to an FP8 KV cache on SM100, halving KV memory per rank with 2.3-5.5% more throughput at a 7-11% TTFT cost in the PR's benchmark (#60140, #60281); fp8_ds_mla on SM90 gives GLM-5.3-Flash up to 31% more output throughput (#59246); ROCm gains the 4-bit ultraquant_4bit KV cache with about 2x the density of FP8 (#57057).
  • Model Runner V2: a GPU n-gram speculator with variable-length drafts (#40704), Elastic EP (#53934), pipeline parallelism with prefill context parallelism for MLA models (#59139), a stock torch.compile mode (#59079), and MRV2 is now the default on ROCm with the model-specific MRV1 exceptions removed (#56360).
  • Faster startup and serving: vllm download-kernels installs FlashInfer's precompiled kernels (#58765); vllm preload --preload-autotune keeps the FlashInfer autotune table warm across restarts (#60085); a shared-memory tensor arena broadcasts large multimodal tensors to workers with one copy (#51207); tokenizers and processors load from the local snapshot (#60825); and with --api-server-count above 1 each connection goes to the least-loaded API worker, for 43-85% more req/s on short requests (Qwen3-0.6B, 32 input / 1 output tokens) in the PR's benchmark (#60723).
  • Model support: new EmbeddingGemma 2 omni-modal embeddings (#60254), MiniCPM-V 4.7 (#58674) and Nemotron 3.5 ASR (#59827); video input in the Transformers modeling backend (#57441); GLM-5.3 sparse MLA index conversions reused across layers (3.5-3.9x on that kernel, #59464) and fused multi-step draft decode (13.3% at concurrency 1, #57443); HiSparse per-request residency caching for up to 58% more throughput on GLM-5.3-NVFP4 on B200 with long, fully GPU-resident contexts at high concurrency (#60083).
  • Security: fixes for GHSA-4hhp-h66f-j5j7 (chat template resource exhaustion, #50300), GHSA-q97c-p368-75c4 (tokenizer max_token_id, #59491) and GHSA-frvg-qw88-hww9 (P2P ZMQ socket exhaustion, #51504); CORS no longer allows every origin by default (#61009); untrusted images are limited to raster formats (#60022); shared-memory multimodal cache handles are signed (#59357); and JSON schemas nested deeper than 64 levels are rejected (#60036).
  • Breaking changes: Python 3.10 dropped (#60402); default CORS origins restricted (#61009); transformers>=5.16.1,<5.20.0 and tokenizers>=0.23.2 (#57387, #59796); torch.compile sequence parallelism and AsyncTP passes removed (#60517); cascade attention removed (#61126); mamba_cache_mode="all" removed (#58997); max_tokens no longer reserved from the context window (#57035); Responses API reasoning stream events renamed (#59652).

  • DeepSeek-V4 and V4.1: decoder-side SWA bounded replay (#58132) with replay layers in CUDA graphs and trimmed in PIECEWISE graphs (compilation_config.decoder_replay_trim_threshold, #59532) plus last KV-source layer trimming (+3.6%, #59894), packed FP8 Engram exchange across DP (#59923), faster CPU-offloaded Engram lookups (#59327), fused DeepSeek V4 + MTP drafting (#58463), encoder CUDA graph packing for V4.1 and Kimi-K3 (11% lower mean TTFT, #58925), EPLB for DSpark drafts (#57549), and fixes for NVFP4 checkpoints with 0% draft acceptance (#59655), MegaMoE shared-expert finalize ordering (#59927), worst-case vision dummy inputs (#57898, #59271), compressor ring null-block writes (#58560), Triton 3.9 indexer quantization (#60716) and decoder-replay CUDA graphs with FlashInfer EP MoE backends (#61041).
  • Qwen: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (Qwen4Exp) merged QSA projections in one GEMM (1.45-1.68x, #59533), fused QSA pre-indexer (#57097), sequence parallelism through --enable-hc-sp (#56322), SM100 low-latency decode GEMM plans (up to 2.7x vs cuBLAS on small-M, #59214), --kv-cache-dtype-skip-layers honored (#60023), and PLE loading for INC (#59990), Quark (#59443) and pre-SM89 GPUs (#60142); Qwen3-VL/Qwen3.5/Qwen3.8 M-RoPE cache 4x smaller and Qwen3.5 YaRN matching Transformers (#59853); Qwen3-Omni M-RoPE fixes (#58890, #59842); Qwen3-ASR on the upstream processor (#57146); Qwen3-VL unknown video fps (#60501) and per-video options with the multimodal cache (#55203).
  • Kimi-K3 and MiniMax-M3: Kimi-K3 FlashInfer fused speculative KDA on SM100 (#54255), fused vision processor (10-20x preprocessing at 1080p-8K, #59278), fused K/V pack on the DCP prefill path (#56881), and DSpark KV cache back to 4 groups (#59733); MiniMax-M3 MSA prefill with an E4M3 query (26-37% faster with FP8 KV, #60684), FP8 indexer cache on non-SM100 GPUs (#59081), Triton indexer tuning (#56151, #59481), and indexer score fixes (#60194, #54597).

Engine Core

  • Model Runner V2: GPU n-gram speculator (#40704), Elastic EP with drain-then-commit scaling (#53934), PP with PCP for MLA models (#59139), STOCK_TORCH_COMPILE mode (#59079), dynamic K in autoregressive speculators (#57053), MTP sampling-mask replay (#59359) and per-module LM heads (#58921), non-blocking H2D copies on WSL2 (#60215), and fixes for int64 index offsets at long context (#60736), warmup (#61013), GDN prefill checkpoints (#59536) and MRV2+PP+MTP align state (#60210).
  • Speculative decoding: fused multi-step draft decode on FlashInfer trtllm-gen (#58371), FlashInfer ReplaySSM for Mamba2 MTP (#52928), in-graph metadata for DFlash/DSpark drafts (#60692), and correctness fixes for ngram on hybrid recurrent models (#56531), Mamba prefill checkpoints with MTP and prefix caching (#59759, #60797), stop-string trimming (#47616), draft model config (#61240), adaptive block verification (#60945), DSpark bonus slots (#59105) and draft models on the Transformers backend (#59293).
  • Hybrid models and prefix caching: Mamba2 internal prefill checkpoints for NemotronH, Granite-4.0-H, Falcon-H1 and Zamba2 (#57329), stale block hashes dropped when streaming sessions truncate (#59103), and fixes for quantized Mamba-2 with TP (#58083), spec decode page sizes (#59975), prefix-cache bounds (#55601, #60533) and sm90 Mamba2 NaNs (#61718).
  • Sleep and RL: sleep releases workspace scratch (up to 4.5 GiB/GPU, #59156) and KV-init state (about 4.6 GiB/GPU, #59158), opt-in sleep_mode_offload_cudagraph (#59160, #59523); token-level weight-version spans on outputs (#59582, #61070); weight-transfer communicators released without stopping inference (#61060); --sleep-preserve-parameter-names 'draft.*' (#61046); modelexpress weight-transfer backend (#58399); POST /weight_checker (#51350); weight-transfer metrics (#55781); --enable-nccl-comm-suspend releasing the MNNVL workspace (#59360); and sleep(level=2) keeping FP8 KV scales (#57163).
  • HiSparse: per-request residency cache (up to 58% at high concurrency with GPU-resident contexts, #60083), lower scheduler overhead (#57930), GPU residency owned by HiSparse (#60647), less staging memory (#60429), host cache gauges (#58949, #59485), and fixes for decode token limits (#60682) and TP hangs (#60941).
  • Startup and memory: shared-memory tensor arena (--enable-shm-tensor-arena, on by default, #51207), Fast Start with PP (#55477), daemon-held weights counted against gpu_memory_utilization (#57298), autotune preload (#60085), local tokenizer snapshots (#60825), sparse_mla_prefill_workspace_factor saving several GiB at 1M context (#61023), cached memory reclaimed during weight loading (#57516), fewer Triton sampler warmup compiles (#58605), sharded state loader with PP (#52110), and reload_weights with Run:ai streamer (#58124).
  • Kernels and runtime: MoE weighted-sum tuning (1.17-2.37x, #59731), flash-maxsim kernels for ColBERT/ColPali scoring (#40337), fallback detokenization with 69% less CPU at 32K tokens (#60497), faster KV block free queue (#60269), Triton kernels off tl.make_block_ptr (#60502), fusion passes restored under PyTorch 2.15 (#57299) and static FP8 quant fusion on recent torch (#61108).
  • Batch invariance: custom all-reduce under VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 (#58623), deterministic split-K LoRA shrink (#59377), every attention backend checked (#60271), SM120 TP configs (#58495), and ROCm support (#52231).

Security

  • GHSA-4hhp-h66f-j5j7: chat templates are validated statically and rendered under a timeout (VLLM_CHAT_TEMPLATE_RENDER_TIMEOUT), user-supplied chat_template in Responses chat_template_kwargs is rejected, and the Rust frontend caps template execution (#50300).
  • GHSA-q97c-p368-75c4: tokenizer max_token_id off-by-one fixed (#59491).
  • GHSA-frvg-qw88-hww9: P2P ZMQ peer sessions are bounded by VLLM_P2P_MAX_PEERS (default 128), VLLM_P2P_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_S (default 30) and VLLM_P2P_IDLE_TIMEOUT_S (default 300), so unique peer addresses can no longer exhaust ZMQ sockets (#51504).
  • Default CORS settings no longer allow every origin in the Python and Rust frontends; set --allowed-origins to permit browser origins (#61009).
  • Untrusted images are opened with a raster-format allowlist (ALLOWED_IMAGE_FORMATS), denying EPS/PostScript and WMF (#60022); shared-memory multimodal cache handles are HMAC-signed and forged handles rejected (#59357).
  • Structured-output JSON schemas nested more than 64 levels return 400 (#60036); chunked /v1/embeddings requests keep cache_salt (#47696); Phi-4 MM audio no longer holds multi-GiB attention matrices (#60614); DeepSeek-OCR zero-sum pixel tensors no longer kill EngineCore (#59417).
  • Security dependency bumps: aiohttp>=3.14.3, pillow>=12.3.0, cryptography, urllib3, pyjwt and others (#59249, #59315, #59427).

Build

  • Python 3.11-3.14 supported (#60402); macOS wheels built with the stable ABI (#60312); CUDA source builds require GCC 13 and fail early otherwise (#60259); Docker images compile Python bytecode at build time for faster container startup (#55422); VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED finds a compatible published wheel within the last 20 commits (#58871); the vendored DeepGEMM uses TORCH_LIBRARY (abi3, #48962).

Breaking Changes & Deprecations

  • Python 3.10 is no longer supported; the minimum is Python 3.11 (#60402).
  • Default CORS origins changed from * to none; set --allowed-origins for browser clients (#61009).
  • transformers>=5.16.1,<5.20.0 and tokenizers>=0.23.2 are required (#57387, #59796).
  • The torch.compile sequence parallelism and AsyncTP passes were removed, along with PassConfig.enable_sp, fuse_gemm_comms and sp_min_token_num; model-level sequence parallelism is unaffected (#60517).
  • Cascade attention was removed; --disable-cascade-attn still parses but only warns and will be removed in v0.33.0 (#61126).
  • mamba_cache_mode="all" was removed; --mamba-cache-mode all now fails validation (#58997).
  • Previously deprecated APIs were removed: wait_for_inflight_requests (use mode="wait"), AsyncLLM.pause_generation(), IOProcessor.output_to_response, vllm.scripts.main() and vllm bench throughput --dataset (#60923). The sonnet benchmark dataset was removed as scheduled (#60129). Tensorizer support was removed from LoRA (#60024), and the PyO3 vllm._rust_tool_parser bridge was removed (#59744).
  • API changes: max_tokens is treated as an upper bound on output rather than reserved from the context window (#57035); Responses API streaming uses response.content_part.added/done with part.type="reasoning_text" instead of response.reasoning_part.added/done (#59652); SamplingParams.prompt_logprob_token_ids is per row (#56984); /inference/v1/generate logprobs use integer token IDs (#58181); sleep API responses are standardized and invalid levels return 400 (#52864); return_mm_kwargs is deprecated in favor of mm_payload (#61427).
  • Watermarking: when the engine has watermarking configured, an omitted request field means enabled and only false opts out; unsupported combinations warn and fall back (#56801).
  • Rust frontend: qwen3_xml now parses Qwen3-Coder XML (alias of qwen3_coder); use the new qwen3_json for the JSON format (#60136).
  • New defaults: shared-memory tensor arena on (#51207); GLM-5.x FP8 KV cache on SM100 with --kv-cache-dtype auto (#60140, #60281); VLLM_DEEPEP_V2_ALLOW_HYBRID_MODE=1 (#57991); Humming preferred over Marlin on SM90 (#56997); sparse_mla_prefill_workspace_factor 2 above 256K max_model_len (#61023); MRV2 on ROCm with model-specific MRV1 exceptions removed (#56360); VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_DCP_VERIFY=auto (#59965); dtype=auto picks bfloat16 on PowerPC (#58528); MXFP4 W4A4 checkpoints fall back to W4A16 with a warning when no W4A4 kernel exists (#60079).
  • Stricter validation: incompatible --prefix-match-unit (#58021), max_num_scheduled_tokens=0 (#60714), HiSparse with cudagraph_mode=FULL (#59688), and negative --device-ids (#49053) are rejected at startup.

title: Release 2.73.0 corresponding to NGC container 26.09
summary:
Triton Inference Server

The Triton Inference Server provides a cloud inferencing solution optimized for both CPUs and GPUs. The server provides an inference service via an HTTP or GRPC endpoint, allowing remote clients to request inferencing for any model being managed by the server. For edge deployments, Triton Server is also available as a shared library with an API that allows the full functionality of the server to be included directly in an application.

New Features and Improvements

  • The 26.09 DLFW containers introduce initial support for the NVIDIA Rubin GPU architecture.
  • Core: Flagged the developer_tools C API wrapper as deprecated in the documentation.
  • Client: Fixed reading of cudaIpcMemHandle_t bytes via getPtr() for compatibility with cuda-bindings 13.x.
  • Restored preserve_ordering behavior by reserving the completion-queue slot at enqueue time.
  • Fixed default_model_filename autofill incorrectly applying to Python-runtime PyTorch models.
  • OpenVINO backend: Fixed the OpenVINO GPU plugin build to ship libOpenCL.so.1.
  • Python backend: Fixed a segfault during shutdown when using Triton metrics, and fixed shared-memory cleanup on forced shutdown.
  • PyTorch backend: Fixed swapped ReportStatistics timestamp arguments and added a guard to the AOTI package loader in the PT2/AOTI backend.
  • Excluded libtritonserver from auditwheel processing in the tritonfrontend wheel build.
  • Fixed a crash: shared-memory inference requests now return a graceful UNAVAILABLE error instead of a NULL-dereference crash.
  • SageMaker integration: Fixed cross-model invoke/unload handling for multi-model endpoints.
  • OpenAI-compatible frontend: Improved cancellation handling for response streams.
  • Fixed an unhandled exception when parsing inference header length in the HTTP frontends.
  • Build: Updated the C++ standard from C++17 to C++20.
  • Build: Migrated the tritonfrontend wheel to hatchling with PEP 639 metadata.

Known Issues

  • The Triton TensorRT-LLM Backend container image is not included in this release.
  • vLLM's v0 API and Ray are affected by vulnerabilities. Users should consider their own architecture and mitigation steps which may include but should not be limited to:
    • Do not expose Ray executors and vLLM hosts to a network where any untrusted connections might reach the host.
    • Ensure that only the other vLLM hosts are able to connect to the TCP port used for the XPUB socket. Note that the port used is random.
  • When using Valgrind or other leak detection tools on AGX-Thor or DGX-Spark systems, you might see memory leaks attributed to NvRmGpuLibOpen.
  • Valgrind or other memory leak detection tools may occasionally report leaks related to DCGM. These reports are intermittent and often disappear on retry.
  • CuPy has issues with the CUDA 13 Device API in multithreaded contexts. Avoid using tritonclient cuda_shared_memory APIs in multithreaded environments until fixed by CuPy.
  • TensorRT calibration cache may require size adjustment in some cases, which was observed for the IGX platform.
  • The core Python binding may incur an additional D2H and H2D copy if the backend and frontend both specify device memory to be used for response tensors.
  • A segmentation fault related to DCGM and NSCQ may be encountered during server shutdown on NVSwitch systems. A possible workaround for this issue is to disable the collection of GPU metrics tritonserver --allow-gpu-metrics false ....
  • When using TensorRT models, if auto-complete configuration is disabled and is_non_linear_format_io:true for reformat-free tensors is not provided in the model configuration, the model may not load successfully.
  • When using Python models in decoupled mode, users need to ensure that the ResponseSender goes out of scope or is properly cleaned up before unloading the model to guarantee that the unloading process executes correctly.
  • Triton Inference Server with vLLM backend currently does not support running vLLM models with tensor parallelism sizes greater than 1 and the default "distributed_executor_backend" setting when using explicit model control mode. In attempt to load a vllm model (tp > 1) in explicit mode, users could potentially see failure at initialize step: could not acquire lock for <_io.BufferedWriter name='<stdout>'> at interpreter shutdown, possibly due to daemon threads. For the default model control mode, after server shutdown, vllm related sub-processes are not killed. Related vllm issue: vllm-project/vllm#6766. Please specify "distributed_executor_backend":"ray" in the model.json when deploying vllm models with tensor parallelism > 1.
  • When loading models with file override, multiple model configuration files are not supported. Users must provide the model configuration by setting parameter "config" : "<JSON>" instead of custom configuration file in the following format: "file:configs/<model-config-name>.pbtxt" : "<base64-encoded-file-content>".
  • TensorRT-LLM backend provides limited support of Triton extensions and features.
  • The TensorRT-LLM backend may core dump on server shutdown. This impacts server teardown only and will not impact inferencing.
  • The Java CAPI is known to have intermittent segfaults.
  • Some systems which implement malloc() may not release memory back to the operating system right away causing a false memory leak. This can be mitigated by using a different malloc implementation. Tcmalloc and jemalloc are installed in the Triton container and can be used by specifying the library in LD_PRELOAD. NVIDIA recommends experimenting with both tcmalloc and jemalloc to determine which one works better for your use case.
  • Auto-complete may cause an increase in server start time. To avoid a start time increase, users can provide the full model configuration and launch the server with --disable-auto-complete-config.
  • Auto-complete does not support PyTorch models due to lack of metadata in the model. It can only verify that the number of inputs and the input names matches what is specified in the model configuration. There is no model metadata about the number of outputs and datatypes. Related PyTorch bug: pytorch/pytorch#38273
  • Triton Client PIP wheels for ARM SBSA are not available from PyPI and pip will install an incorrect Jetson version of Triton Client library for Arm SBSA. The correct client wheel file can be pulled directly from the Arm SBSA SDK image and manually installed.
  • Traced models in PyTorch seem to create overflows when int8 tensor values are transformed to int32 on the GPU. Refer to pytorch/pytorch#66930 for more information.
  • Triton cannot retrieve GPU metrics with MIG-enabled GPU devices.
  • Triton metrics might not work if the host machine is running a separate DCGM agent on bare-metal or in a container.

Client Libraries and Examples

The client libraries and examples are available in this release exclusively via the Ubuntu 24.04–based NGC Container. The SDK container includes the client libraries and examples, Performance Analyzer, and Model Analyzer. See Getting the Client Libraries for more information.

ManyLinux Assets (early access)

This release was compiled with AlmaLinux 8.9 based out of manylinux_2_34 and can be used on RHEL 9 and later versions.
See the included README.md for complete details about installation, verification, and support.
This release supports ensembles. Confirm CUDA, TensorRT, ONNX Runtime, PyTorch, and Python versions in the shipped README.md.
Some optional backend features such as the PyTorch backend's TorchTRT extension are not currently supported.

title: Release 2.70.0 corresponding to NGC container 26.06
summary:
Triton Inference Server

The Triton Inference Server provides a cloud inferencing solution optimized for both CPUs and GPUs. The server provides an inference service via an HTTP or GRPC endpoint, allowing remote clients to request inferencing for any model being managed by the server. For edge deployments, Triton Server is also available as a shared library with an API that allows the full functionality of the server to be included directly in an application.

New Features and Improvements

  • (Breaking) Removed deprecated Windows support: Dropped the Windows server build and removed Windows from the core build and documentation.
  • (Breaking) Python client BF16 handling: The client now requires ml_dtypes.bfloat16 arrays for BF16 input/output tensors and no longer casts to/from np.float32. Scripts that passed BF16 data as np.float32 arrays must switch to ml_dtypes.bfloat16.
  • TensorRT backend: Added multi-device (multi-GPU) inference support.
  • PyTorch backend: Enabled PyTorch 2 dynamic batching.
  • OpenAI-compatible frontend: Added an HTTP request body size limit.
  • Fixed a server crash when loading models from S3 after an idle-connection timeout.
  • Security: Hardened model environment unpacking and file-path handling against path traversal.
  • Improved request validation in the SageMaker endpoint.

  • Fixed a server crash caused by improper error handling.

  • Avoid the specific APIs/flows (low-level OCB, BIO_f_linebuffer with short writes, CMS password-based decryption, low-level GF(2^m) with untrusted params) for many linux binaries, in order to avoid exposure to known issues in OpenSSL 1.1.1.
  • vLLM's v0 API and Ray are affected by vulnerabilities. Users should consider their own architecture and mitigation steps which may include but should not be limited to:
    • Do not expose Ray executors and vLLM hosts to a network where any untrusted connections might reach the host.
    • Ensure that only the other vLLM hosts are able to connect to the TCP port used for the XPUB socket. Note that the port used is random.
  • When using Valgrind or other leak detection tools on AGX-Thor or DGX-Spark systems, you might see memory leaks attributed to NvRmGpuLibOpen.
  • Valgrind or other memory leak detection tools may occasionally report leaks related to DCGM. These reports are intermittent and often disappear on retry.
  • CuPy has issues with the CUDA 13 Device API in multithreaded contexts. Avoid using tritonclient cuda_shared_memory APIs in multithreaded environments until fixed by CuPy.
  • TensorRT calibration cache may require size adjustment in some cases, which was observed for the IGX platform.
  • The core Python binding may incur an additional D2H and H2D copy if the backend and frontend both specify device memory to be used for response tensors.
  • A segmentation fault related to DCGM and NSCQ may be encountered during server shutdown on NVSwitch systems. A possible workaround for this issue is to disable the collection of GPU metrics tritonserver --allow-gpu-metrics false ....
  • When using TensorRT models, if auto-complete configuration is disabled and is_non_linear_format_io:true for reformat-free tensors is not provided in the model configuration, the model may not load successfully.
  • When using Python models in decoupled mode, users need to ensure that the ResponseSender goes out of scope or is properly cleaned up before unloading the model to guarantee that the unloading process executes correctly.
  • Triton Inference Server with vLLM backend currently does not support running vLLM models with tensor parallelism sizes greater than 1 and the default "distributed_executor_backend" setting when using explicit model control mode. In attempt to load a vllm model (tp > 1) in explicit mode, users could potentially see failure at initialize step: could not acquire lock for <_io.BufferedWriter name='<stdout>'> at interpreter shutdown, possibly due to daemon threads. For the default model control mode, after server shutdown, vllm related sub-processes are not killed. Related vllm issue: vllm-project/vllm#6766. Please specify "distributed_executor_backend":"ray" in the model.json when deploying vllm models with tensor parallelism > 1.
  • When loading models with file override, multiple model configuration files are not supported. Users must provide the model configuration by setting parameter "config" : "<JSON>" instead of custom configuration file in the following format: "file:configs/<model-config-name>.pbtxt" : "<base64-encoded-file-content>".
  • TensorRT-LLM backend provides limited support of Triton extensions and features.
  • The TensorRT-LLM backend may core dump on server shutdown. This impacts server teardown only and will not impact inferencing.
  • The Java CAPI is known to have intermittent segfaults.
  • Some systems which implement malloc() may not release memory back to the operating system right away causing a false memory leak. This can be mitigated by using a different malloc implementation. Tcmalloc and jemalloc are installed in the Triton container and can be used by specifying the library in LD_PRELOAD. NVIDIA recommends experimenting with both tcmalloc and jemalloc to determine which one works better for your use case.
  • Auto-complete may cause an increase in server start time. To avoid a start time increase, users can provide the full model configuration and launch the server with --disable-auto-complete-config.
  • Auto-complete does not support PyTorch models due to lack of metadata in the model. It can only verify that the number of inputs and the input names matches what is specified in the model configuration. There is no model metadata about the number of outputs and datatypes. Related PyTorch bug: pytorch/pytorch#38273
  • Triton Client PIP wheels for ARM SBSA are not available from PyPI and pip will install an incorrect Jetson version of Triton Client library for Arm SBSA. The correct client wheel file can be pulled directly from the Arm SBSA SDK image and manually installed.
  • Traced models in PyTorch seem to create overflows when int8 tensor values are transformed to int32 on the GPU. Refer to pytorch/pytorch#66930 for more information.
  • Triton cannot retrieve GPU metrics with MIG-enabled GPU devices.
  • Triton metrics might not work if the host machine is running a separate DCGM agent on bare-metal or in a container.

The client libraries and examples are available in this release exclusively via the Ubuntu 24.04–based NGC Container. The SDK container includes the client libraries and examples, Performance Analyzer, and Model Analyzer. See Getting the Client Libraries for more information.

title: Release 2.66.0 corresponding to NGC container 26.02
summary:
Triton Inference Server

The Triton Inference Server provides a cloud inferencing solution optimized for both CPUs and GPUs. The server provides an inference service via an HTTP or GRPC endpoint, allowing remote clients to request inferencing for any model being managed by the server. For edge deployments, Triton Server is also available as a shared library with an API that allows the full functionality of the server to be included directly in an application.

Important

Triton 26.02 is the last Triton release for Jetson platform devices on GitHub.

New Features and Improvements

  • Fixed and updated broken links and anchors in documents across repositories.

  • Fixed broken page links on Nvidia Triton Inference Server Documentation.

  • Fixed an issue where unbound output size from a model could lead to resource exhaustion and denial of service. (#8603)

  • Fixed an issue where malformed HTTP header could cause a server crash (#8637)

Known Issues

  • Avoid the specific APIs/flows (low-level OCB, BIO_f_linebuffer with short writes, CMS password-based decryption, low-level GF(2^m) with untrusted params) for Manylinux binaries, in order to avoid exposure to known issues in OpenSSL 1.1.1.

  • Since 25.10, vLLM backend uses V1 engine by default. You might see invalid characters in logprobs output and the bug has been reported to the vLLM team.

  • PyTorch backend supports PyTorch 2.0 with the limitation that models must be provided as a serialized model file (aka ‘model.pt’). Please see Triton PyTorch Backend documentation for details.

  • vLLM's v0 API and Ray are affected by vulnerabilities. Users should consider their own architecture and mitigation steps which may include but should not be limited to:

    • Do not expose Ray executors and vLLM hosts to a network where any untrusted connections might reach the host.
    • Ensure that only the other vLLM hosts are able to connect to the TCP port used for the XPUB socket. Note that the port used is random.

  • When using Valgrind or other leak detection tools on AGX-Thor or DGX-Spark systems, you might see memory leaks attributed to NvRmGpuLibOpen. The root cause has been identified and fixed in CUDA.

  • Valgrind or other memory leak detection tools may occasionally report leaks related to DCGM. These reports are intermittent and often disappear on retry. The root cause is under investigation.

  • CuPy has issues with the CUDA 13 Device API in multithreaded contexts. Avoid using tritonclient cuda_shared_memory APIs in multithreaded environments until fixed by CuPy.

  • TensorRT calibration cache may require size adjustment in some cases, which was observed for the IGX platform.

  • The core Python binding may incur an additional D2H and H2D copy if the backend and frontend both specify device memory to be used for response tensors.

  • A segmentation fault related to DCGM and NSCQ may be encountered during server shutdown on NVSwitch systems. A possible workaround for this issue is to disable the collection of GPU metrics tritonserver --allow-gpu-metrics false ...

  • When using TensorRT models, if auto-complete configuration is disabled and is_non_linear_format_io:true for reformat-free tensors is not provided in the model configuration, the model may not load successfully.

  • When using Python models in decoupled mode, users need to ensure that the ResponseSender goes out of scope or is properly cleaned up before unloading the model to guarantee that the unloading process executes correctly.

  • Triton Inference Server with vLLM backend currently does not support running vLLM models with tensor parallelism sizes greater than 1 and the default "distributed_executor_backend" setting when using explicit model control mode. In attempt to load a vllm model (tp > 1) in explicit mode, users could potentially see failure at initialize step: could not acquire lock for <_io.BufferedWriter name='<stdout>'> at interpreter shutdown, possibly due to daemon threads. For the default model control mode, after server shutdown, vllm related sub-processes are not killed. Related vllm issue: vllm-project/vllm#6766 . Please specify "distributed_executor_backend":"ray" in the model.json when deploying vllm models with tensor parallelism > 1.

  • When loading models with file override, multiple model configuration files are not supported. Users must provide the model configuration by setting parameter "config" : "<JSON>" instead of custom configuration file in the following format: "file:configs/<model-config-name>.pbtxt" : "<base64-encoded-file-content>".

  • TensorRT-LLM backend provides limited support of Triton extensions and features.

  • The TensorRT-LLM backend may core dump on server shutdown. This impacts server teardown only and will not impact inferencing.

  • The Java CAPI is known to have intermittent segfaults.

  • Some systems which implement malloc() may not release memory back to the operating system right away causing a false memory leak. This can be mitigated by using a different malloc implementation. TCMalloc and jemalloc are installed in the Triton container and can be used by specifying the library in LD_PRELOAD. NVIDIA recommends experimenting with both tcmalloc and jemalloc to determine which one works better for your use case.

  • Auto-complete may cause an increase in server start time. To avoid a start time increase, users can provide the full model configuration and launch the server with --disable-auto-complete-config.

  • Auto-complete does not support PyTorch models due to lack of metadata in the model. It can only verify that the number of inputs and the input names matches what is specified in the model configuration. There is no model metadata about the number of outputs and datatypes. Related PyTorch bug: https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/38273

  • Triton Client PIP wheels for ARM SBSA are not available from PyPI and pip will install an incorrect Jetson version of Triton Client library for Arm SBSA. The correct client wheel file can be pulled directly from the Arm SBSA SDK image and manually installed.

  • Traced models in PyTorch seem to create overflows when int8 tensor values are transformed to int32 on the GPU. Refer to pytorch/pytorch#66930 for more information.

  • Triton cannot retrieve GPU metrics with MIG-enabled GPU devices.

  • Triton metrics might not work if the host machine is running a separate DCGM agent on bare-metal or in a container.

Client Libraries and Examples

Ubuntu 24.04 builds of the client libraries and examples are included in this release in the attached v2.66.0_ubuntu2404.clients.tar.gz file. The SDK is also available for as an Ubuntu 24.04 based NGC Container. The SDK container includes the client libraries and examples, Performance Analyzer and Model Analyzer. Some components are also available in the tritonclient pip package. See Getting the Client Libraries for more information on each of these options.

Jetson iGPU Support

A release of Triton for IGX is provided in the attached tar file: tritonserver2.66.0-igpu.tar.

  • This release supports CUDA 12.9, TensorRT 10.11.0.33, Onnx Runtime 1.24.1, PyTorch [2.11.0a0+eb65b36](https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/frameworks/install-pytorch-jetson-platform-release-notes/pytorch-jetson-rel.html), **Python** 3.12` and as well as ensembles.
  • ONNX Runtime backend does not support the OpenVINO and TensorRT execution providers. The CUDA execution provider is in Beta.
  • System shared memory is supported on Jetson. CUDA shared memory is not supported.
  • GPU metrics, GCS storage, S3 storage and Azure storage are not supported.

The tar file contains the Triton server executable and shared libraries and also the C++ and Python client libraries and examples. For more information on how to install and use Triton on JetPack refer to jetson.md.

The wheel for the Python client library is present in the tar file and can be installed by running the following command:

python3 -m pip install --upgrade clients/python/tritonclient-2.66.0-py3-none-manylinux2014_aarch64.whl[all]

  • This release supports CUDA 13.1, TensorRT 10.15.1.29, Onnx Runtime 1.24.1, PyTorch 2.11.0a0+eb65b36, Python 3.12 and as well as ensembles.

  • This package is a subset of nvcr.io/nvidia/tritonserver:26.02-py3 ARM container image assets it.

Please refer to the support matrix and compatibility.md for all dependency versions related to 25.10. However, the packages listed below have different versions than those specified in the support matrix.

Dependency Version

TensorRT 10.13.3.9

title: v0.14.24
summary:
Release Notes

[2026-08-19]

llama-index-core [0.14.24]

  • fix: close HotpotQA evaluator file handles (#22113)
  • fix(core): preserve oversized leaf nodes in CodeSplitter (#22119)
  • fix: preserve multiblock chat history writes (#22124)
  • fix(core): skip empty nodes in HTMLNodeParser (#22125)
  • fix(core): respect mmr_threshold=0 in MMR embedding search (#22126)
  • fix: keep all nodes per document in IngestionPipeline upserts (re-submit of #22046, not a dup of #21456) (#22133)
  • fix: don't mark *args/**kwargs as required tool parameters (#22135)
  • fix(core): default MetadataFilters condition to AND when None (#22155)
  • fix: honor agent structured_output_fn/output_cls inside AgentWorkflow (#22162)
  • fix(core): use word tokenization for stopword removal in SemanticDoubleMergingSplitterNodeParser (#22167)
  • fix(core): restore prompt helper fallback to supplied LLM metadata (#22177)
  • populate response text on streaming chat response when writing to memory (#22179)
  • feat(property_graph): add raise_on_error to LLM path extractors (#22195)
  • Clarify FactExtractionMemoryBlock condense prompt to return a full snapshot (#22213)
  • fix a few typos (#22512)
  • fix(core): give each CitationQueryEngine citation node its own id and offsets (#22537)
  • fix(core): persist SimpleChatStore without escaping non-ascii (#22538)
  • feat(core): allow Memory to accept any AsyncDBChatStore (#22541)
  • test(node_parser): enable pytest discovery for sentence_window tests (#22545)
  • Implement async for LLMRerank (#22597)

llama-index-embeddings-bedrock [0.8.3]

  • fix: make aioboto3 optional in llama-index-embeddings-bedrock (#21915)
  • fix(embeddings): validate non-empty Bedrock embedding payload before AWS call (#22527)

llama-index-embeddings-voyageai [0.6.1]

  • fix: set chunk_size=32000 and fix input format for contextualizedembeddings (#22144)

llama-index-graph-stores-falkordb [0.6.0]

  • fix(falkordb): correct schema, vector ranking, filters and batching in property graph store (#22522)

llama-index-indices-managed-dashscope [0.5.1]

  • fix(dashscope): send query_history in retriever payload (#22212)

llama-index-indices-managed-lancedb [0.3.2]

  • fix(lancedb): repair image ingestion crash, embedding_model typo, and… (#22544)
  • lint (#22572)

llama-index-llms-anthropic [0.11.10]

  • feat(anthropic): Add support for Claude Sonnet 5 (#22202)

title: langgraph==1.2.16
summary:
Changes since 1.2.15

  • release(langgraph): 1.2.16 (#9334)
  • fix(langgraph): let other tasks finish when a resume value is invalid (#9265)
  • fix(langgraph): apply a resumed Command's update once (#9322)
  • fix(langgraph): stop a subgraph from rerunning its finished tasks on resume (#9315)
  • fix(langgraph): save a resumed exit run's pending writes once (#9314)
  • release(prebuilt): 1.1.1 (#9316)
  • release(checkpoint-postgres): 3.2.0 (#9313)
  • feat(checkpoint-postgres): add prune to PostgresSaver and AsyncPostgresSaver (#9290)
  • fix(langgraph): keep a DeltaChannel's value when its field changes to a plain reducer (#9302)
  • release(checkpoint-postgres): 3.1.3 (#9287)
  • release(checkpoint-sqlite): 3.1.2 (#9288)

New Features

  • Added keyboard-driven transcript selection with word, line, and page motions, integrated search, and configurable shortcuts. (#57221, #57222, #57223, #57224)
  • Rendered Markdown consistently in async questions, choices, answers, and transcript replies. (#57259, #57292)
  • Added GPT-6.1 Terra to the bundled, Vertex AI, and Amazon Bedrock model catalogs. (#57293)
  • Added codex queue --resume to resume unloaded threads after queueing a message. (#57232)
  • Added clearer safety-block explanations and selectable safer follow-up prompts in the TUI. (#57363, #57365)
  • Added codex doctor --network-only for focused configuration, connectivity, and WebSocket diagnostics. (#57606)

Bug Fixes

  • Preserved acknowledged approval and permission settings when resuming or forking threads. (#57227)
  • Preserved local image attachments when restoring killed composer text. (#57502)
  • Fixed standalone release cleanup on macOS when installations are in use or paths contain non-ASCII characters. (#57503)
  • Restored spawned descendant threads when unarchiving their parent. (#57635)
  • Fixed app-server thread startup and shutdown races and released completed runtimes promptly. (#57787, #57788)
  • Improved TUI reconnection recovery, including offline /quit and /exit handling. (#57820)
  • Preserved reasoning-token accounting across resume and fork to avoid premature compaction. (#57839)

Chores

  • Switched Bazel to source-built V8 with target-matched Rust bindings and native Windows MSVC archive support. (#57164, #57269, #57644, #57832)
  • Shipped the standalone executor in canonical CLI and app-server release packages. (#57837)
  • Standardized development and release builds on Node.js 24.22.1 and Rust 1.95.0. (#57168, #57373)

summary: Release 0.166.0-alpha.1

New Features

  • Added a built-in Google Cloud Vertex AI provider, configured with model_provider = "gcp". (#56265)
  • Added GPT-6.1 Terra to the model catalogs. (#57337)
  • Added a repository filter to the session picker and directory grouping to the agent command center, making it easier to navigate sessions across linked worktrees. (#56308)
  • Added experimental attached thread forks to the app-server API. (#56351)
  • Enabled reasoning effort changes during a conversation by default for supported models. (#56163)
  • Enabled memory v2 by default for fresh profiles and added support for importing external-agent memories into it. (#56211, #56414)

Bug Fixes

  • Fixed fresh TUI sessions to honor the server’s default approval reviewer when no explicit override is provided. (#56090)
  • Kept TUI preferences editable and immediately applicable when execution settings are invalid. (#56091)
  • Cancelled remote MCP tool requests when their local response futures are dropped. (#56132)
  • Prevented queued agent messages from restarting work after an interrupt or a switch to Plan mode. (#56330)
  • Stopped retrying when a provider reports that a model was not found, preserving its error message. (#56445)
  • Closed a marketplace URL validation gap that could allow Git to connect to a different host than the one checked against allowed patterns. (#56263)
